To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a combination of distributed hydrological model and parametrized hydraulic model can provide a good estimate of the flood extent in a region where terrain and hydrological data is scarce.
A distributed hydrological model was calibrated for the Oti River in West Africa and used to drive a hydraulic model for flood extent modelling in a region with limited data availability.
it is possible to model flood hazard in West Africa, even in the absence of data.

the development of an innovative methodology for flood modelling in data-scarce regions, and the application of the methodology to a 140  km reach of the O ti River, West Africa.
the application of hydrological and hydraulic models to a region of West Africa, where data availability is poor.

developing a methodology to simulate flood extent, in a data scarce region, using a combination of a calibrated hydrological model and a hydraulic model, with the latter calibrated to a flood extent survey.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible to model the flood hazard extent for this region with freely available data and a distributed hydrological and sub-grid hydraulic modelling approach.
the flood extent model fit was good, given the data scarcity, and that this model could be used to predict the likely extent of a flood in this region, given a discharge forecast.

The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to model flood extent in regions where data is scarce and the terrain digital elevation is coarse, but the model fit will be limited.
the combination of a distributed hydrological model and a parametrized, 2D hydraulic model can provide a good estimate of flood extent in data poor regions, such as West Africa.

it is possible to develop a distributed flood model in regions where there are few gauges and little terrain data, but it will likely be difficult to achieve a very good fit between observed and simulated flood extents.
